title: How many cars passed the crossing from 6 a.m. to noon?
description: The bars of the traffic graph at a Delhi crossing are read with the scale of one hundred vehicles for one unit, and the six hourly counts are added. The sum is checked by adding the units first and multiplying by one hundred.
teaching_notes: One idea: read every bar against the scale, then add all the readings. Watch for adding only the tallest bars or forgetting the short first bar.

video_script.why: The child reads six bars with the scale and adds the readings to get a total.
video_script.substitution: Read each bar against the scale of one hundred vehicles for one unit, then add the six counts.
video_script.anchor: the horizontal bar graph of vehicles passing a busy crossing in Delhi in each hour from six in the morning to noon
video_script.payoff_line: About four thousand four hundred and fifty cars passed through the crossing

final_answer.spoken: about four thousand four hundred and fifty cars passed through the crossing

video_script.design: One idea: read each bar with the scale, then add. The graph stays on the board all video and the bars are added in pairs.
open_questions: The book text gives only the counts 1200, 1000, about 800 (from 1000 + 800 = 1800), about 150 and about 600; the 10 to 11 bar of about 700 is read from the worklist, not from the book text.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the horizontal bar graph of vehicles at a busy crossing in Delhi for the hours 6-7, 7-8, 8-9, 9-10, 10-11, 11-12, with the words 1 unit of length = 100 vehicles

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.graph: the bar graph of vehicles at the crossing appears with six bars
marks.scale: the words 1 unit of length = 100 vehicles appear
marks.ask: a question mark appears over all six bars

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the busy crossing in Delhi.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>The bar graph shows the vehicles that passed in each hour, from six in the morning to noon.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>One unit of length stands for one hundred vehicles.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many cars in all passed through the crossing in these six hours?

beats.on_screen: the graph stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the scale label 1 unit = 100 vehicles; a bar of 8 units is shown with 8 x 100 = 800 vehicles; a bar of 1 and a half units is shown with 150 vehicles

marks.scale: the scale label 1 unit = 100 vehicles appears
marks.eight: a bar of 8 units appears and shows 800 vehicles
marks.half: a short bar of 1 and a half units appears and shows 150 vehicles

narration: <bookmark mark='scale'/>The scale gives the value of each bar. A bar of eight units stands for eight times one hundred. That is eight hundred vehicles.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>A bar that is not a whole number of units works the same way.
<bookmark mark='half'/>A bar of one and a half units stands for one hundred and fifty vehicles.

beats.on_screen: Given: bars read with the scale: 6-7 about 150, 7-8 1200, 8-9 1000, 9-10 about 800, 10-11 about 700, 11-12 about 600 vehicles

marks.early: the readings 150, 1200 and 1000 are written beside the first three bars
marks.late: the readings 800, 700 and 600 are written beside the last three bars

narration: <bookmark mark='early'/>Given, the first three bars read about one hundred and fifty. Then they read one thousand two hundred and one thousand.
<bookmark mark='late'/>The last three read about eight hundred, seven hundred and six hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: the total number of cars from 6 a.m. to noon

marks.find: the words the total number of cars are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the total number of cars in the six hours.

marks.first: the six readings are grouped in pairs
marks.sum1: 150 + 1200 = 1350 is written for the first two bars
marks.second: 1000 + 800 = 1800 is written for the next two bars
marks.third: 700 + 600 = 1300 is written for the last two bars

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, add the six readings in pairs, because small sums are safer to keep right.
<bookmark mark='sum1'/>One hundred and fifty and one thousand two hundred make one thousand three hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='second'/>One thousand and eight hundred make one thousand eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Seven hundred and six hundred make one thousand three hundred.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, add the three pair sums. One thousand three hundred and fifty and one thousand eight hundred make three thousand one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three thousand one hundred and fifty and one thousand three hundred make four thousand four hundred and fifty. That is the total.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check with units. 1.5 + 12 + 10 + 8 + 7 + 6 = 44.5 units; 44.5 x 100 = 4450

marks.units: the six bars are read in units: 1.5, 12, 10, 8, 7 and 6
marks.times: 44.5 x 100 = 4450 is written and matches the pair sums

narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Step three, check by adding the units first. The bars are one and a half, twelve, ten, eight, seven and six units.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>They add up to forty four and a half units.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Forty four and a half times one hundred gives four thousand four hundred and fifty. It matches.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4450 cars passed between 6 a.m. and noon
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>About four thousand four hundred and fifty cars passed through the crossing.
